title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor Low Input
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) detects an unusually low voltage signal from the MAP sensor, indicating a possible vacuum leak or sensor malfunction. This affects fuel delivery and engine performance.
symptoms: Poor acceleration; Rough idle; Reduced fuel economy
actions: Inspect MAP sensor wiring for damage; Check vacuum lines connected to the manifold for leaks; Test or replace MAP sensor

title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor High Input
problem: The ECU detects an unusually high voltage signal from the MAP sensor, suggesting a sensor short or an issue with the manifold pressure reading. This can lead to an incorrect air-fuel mixture.
symptoms: Engine hesitation; Black smoke from exhaust; Increased fuel consumption
actions: Inspect MAP sensor wiring for shorts or damage; Clean sensor port on manifold; Test or replace MAP sensor

title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Low Input
problem: The ECU receives a low voltage signal from the IAT sensor, indicating the intake air temperature is unusually high, which can lead to rich fuel conditions.
symptoms: Hard starting when cold; Increased fuel consumption; Reduced power
actions: Inspect IAT sensor wiring; Clean sensor; Test or replace IAT sensor

title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor High Input
problem: The ECU receives a high voltage signal from the IAT sensor, indicating the intake air temperature is unusually low, which can lead to lean fuel conditions.
symptoms: Engine hesitation; Poor acceleration; Engine running rough
actions: Inspect IAT sensor wiring for shorts; Check for air leaks near sensor; Test or replace IAT sensor

title: Throttle Position Sensor Low Input
problem: The ECU detects an abnormally low voltage signal from the throttle position sensor, indicating a problem with the throttle plate position reading. This directly impacts throttle response.
symptoms: Poor throttle response; Engine stalls at idle; Limp home mode activated
actions: Check TPS wiring and connector; Inspect throttle body for sticking; Test or replace TPS sensor

title: Throttle Position Sensor High Input
problem: The ECU detects an abnormally high voltage signal from the throttle position sensor, indicating a problem with the throttle plate position reading. This can cause unintended acceleration or poor control.
symptoms: High idle RPM; Unintended acceleration; Engine running rough
actions: Check TPS wiring for shorts; Inspect throttle body for sticking; Test or replace TPS sensor

title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1
problem: warning
symptoms: The oxygen sensor consistently reports a low voltage, indicating a lean air-fuel mixture or a faulty sensor circuit. This impacts emissions and fuel efficiency.
actions: Increased fuel consumption; Poor engine performance; MIL illumination
location: Inspect O2 sensor wiring for damage; Check for exhaust leaks before the sensor; Test or replace O2 sensor

title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1
problem: warning
symptoms: The oxygen sensor consistently reports a high voltage, indicating a rich air-fuel mixture or a faulty sensor circuit. This can lead to excessive carbon buildup.
actions: Black smoke from exhaust; Engine running rough; Reduced fuel economy
location: Inspect O2 sensor wiring for shorts; Check for fuel system issues (leaky injector); Test or replace O2 sensor

title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1
problem: warning
symptoms: The ECU detects an issue with the heater circuit for the oxygen sensor, which is essential for the sensor to reach operating temperature quickly. This can delay closed-loop operation.
actions: Increased emissions; Delayed engine warm-up; MIL illumination
location: Check O2 sensor heater fuse; Inspect O2 sensor wiring for continuity; Replace O2 sensor if heater is open circuit

title: System Too Lean (Bank 1)
problem: The ECU determines that the engine is consistently running with too much air or not enough fuel based on O2 sensor readings. This can cause engine damage over time.
symptoms: Lack of power; Engine misfires; Overheating
actions: Check for vacuum leaks (intake manifold
location: hoses); Inspect fuel pressure and fuel filter; Test fuel injectors for clogging

title: System Too Rich (Bank 1)
problem: The ECU determines that the engine is consistently running with too much fuel or not enough air based on O2 sensor readings. This can foul spark plugs and contaminate oil.
symptoms: Black smoke from exhaust; Strong fuel smell; Reduced fuel economy
actions: Check for leaky fuel injector(s); Inspect fuel pressure regulator; Verify O2 sensor readings are accurate

title: Injector Circuit/Open - Cylinder 1
problem: The ECU detects an open circuit or malfunction in the electrical circuit of the fuel injector for cylinder 1, meaning it's not firing correctly.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough running; Loss of power
actions: Check injector wiring and connector; Test injector resistance; Replace fuel injector

title: Fuel Pump Primary Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an issue with the primary control circuit for the fuel pump, preventing it from receiving proper power or ground.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start; No fuel pump prime sound; Stalling
actions: Check fuel pump fuse and relay; Inspect wiring from ECU to fuel pump relay; Test fuel pump relay

title: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit Low
problem: The ECU detects low voltage in the secondary circuit leading to the fuel pump, indicating the pump is not receiving sufficient power to operate correctly.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start; Weak fuel pressure; Engine stalls under load
actions: Check fuel pump power wiring; Test fuel pump for proper operation; Inspect fuel pump ground connection

title: Crankshaft Position Sensor 'A' Circuit
problem: The ECU is not receiving a proper signal from the crankshaft position sensor, which is vital for engine timing and RPM calculation.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start; Intermittent stalling; Loss of RPM signal on dashboard
actions: Inspect CKP sensor wiring and connector; Check sensor for metallic debris; Replace CKP sensor

title: Crankshaft Position Sensor 'A' Circuit Range/Performance
problem: The signal from the crankshaft position sensor is erratic or out of expected range, suggesting an issue with the sensor or the reluctor wheel it reads.
symptoms: Engine misfires; Intermittent power loss; Difficult starting
actions: Inspect CKP sensor mounting and alignment; Check for damage to reluctor wheel; Replace CKP sensor

title: Ignition Coil "A" Primary/Secondary Circuit
problem: The ECU detects a malfunction in the primary or secondary circuit of the ignition coil for cylinder 1, leading to a loss of spark.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough idle; Lack of power
actions: Check ignition coil wiring and connector; Test ignition coil resistance; Replace ignition coil

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor 'A' Malfunction
problem: The ECU is not receiving a reliable signal from the vehicle speed sensor, affecting speedometer readings and various engine control strategies.
symptoms: Speedometer not working; Cruise control (if equipped) inoperative; Erratic shifting (if automatic/AMT)
actions: Inspect VSS wiring and connector; Check VSS mounting; Replace VSS sensor
location: Rear wheel or transmission output shaft

title: Idle Control System Malfunction
affectedPart: Idle Air Control (IAC) Valve / Throttle Body
problem: The ECU detects an issue with the system controlling the engine's idle speed, which can be due to a faulty IAC valve or air leaks.
symptoms: Erratic idle speed; Stalling at idle; Engine surges
actions: Clean IAC valve (if present); Check for vacuum leaks around intake; Inspect throttle body for carbon buildup
location: Side of the throttle body or intake manifold

title: System Voltage Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects that the system voltage is outside the normal operating range, indicating potential issues with the battery or charging system.
symptoms: Dim lights; Difficult starting; Electronic systems malfunction
actions: Test battery voltage and condition; Check alternator output; Inspect charging system wiring

title: System Voltage Low
problem: The ECU detects that the battery voltage is consistently too low, which can prevent proper operation of electronic components and starting the engine.
symptoms: Engine cranks slowly; Dim headlights; Electronic systems failing
actions: Charge battery and re-test; Check rectifier/regulator output; Inspect battery terminals for corrosion

title: System Voltage High
problem: The ECU detects that the system voltage is consistently too high, which can damage electronic components and overcharge the battery.
symptoms: Bulbs blowing frequently; Battery overheating; Electronic malfunctions
actions: Test rectifier/regulator for overcharging; Check wiring from stator to regulator; Replace rectifier/regulator

title: Internal Control Module Read Only Memory (ROM) Error
problem: A critical internal error has been detected within the ECU's read-only memory, indicating a likely hardware or software fault within the ECU itself.
symptoms: Engine won't start; Multiple systems failing; MIL constantly on
actions: Check ECU power and ground connections; Attempt ECU re-flash (dealer tool); Replace ECU
location: Under seat or behind headlight fairing

title: Malfunction Indicator Lamp (MIL) Control Circuit
problem: The ECU detects an issue with the circuit that controls the Malfunction Indicator Lamp on the dashboard, meaning the light might not illuminate when required.
symptoms: MIL not illuminating at key on; MIL not illuminating for other faults; Unclear diagnostic status
actions: Check MIL bulb/LED; Inspect wiring to MIL; Check dashboard cluster connections

title: Transmission Control System Malfunction (General)
affectedPart: Transmission Control Module (TCM) / Gear Position Sensor
problem: The ECU detects a general fault within the transmission control system. While most REs are manual, some newer ones might have gear position sensors or other transmission-related electronics.
symptoms: Incorrect gear indication; Difficulty shifting; Engine performance issues
actions: Check gear position sensor wiring; Inspect transmission fluid (if applicable); Use diagnostic tool for specific TCM codes

title: Lean Angle Sensor Circuit Low Voltage
problem: The ECU receives an abnormally low voltage from the lean angle sensor, indicating a potential sensor malfunction or that the bike is leaning excessively. This can trigger an engine kill.
symptoms: Engine stalling when upright; Engine not starting; MIL illumination
actions: Check LAS sensor orientation and mounting; Inspect LAS wiring; Replace LAS sensor
location: Often under the seat or behind the headlight

title: Lean Angle Sensor Circuit High Voltage
problem: The ECU receives an abnormally high voltage from the lean angle sensor, indicating a potential sensor malfunction or an incorrect signal. This can also trigger an engine kill.
symptoms: Engine stalling when upright; Engine not starting; MIL illumination
actions: Check LAS sensor wiring for shorts; Verify sensor mounting is secure; Replace LAS sensor
location: Often under the seat or behind the headlight

title: ECU Internal Voltage Error
problem: The ECU detects an internal voltage supply problem, which can affect the operation of various sensors and actuators connected to it.
symptoms: Multiple sensor faults; Engine cutting out; Unpredictable behavior
actions: Check main relay and battery connections; Inspect ECU power and ground wiring; Replace ECU
location: Under seat or behind headlight fairing

title: Immo Malfunction / Transponder Key Error
problem: The ECU fails to recognize the transponder key signal, preventing the engine from starting due to the immobilizer system being active.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start; Immobilizer light flashes; Key not recognized
actions: Try spare key; Check transponder antenna around ignition; Have system re-programmed (dealer)

title: EVAP Purge Control Valve Circuit
problem: The ECU detects an electrical circuit malfunction in the Evaporative Emission (EVAP) system's purge control valve. This relates to emissions control.
symptoms: MIL illumination; Slight fuel odor; No noticeable driveability issues
actions: Check purge valve wiring and connector; Test purge valve resistance; Replace purge valve
location: Near the fuel tank or charcoal canister

title: EVAP Purge Control Valve Circuit Low
problem: The ECU detects a low voltage condition in the EVAP purge control valve circuit, indicating a potential open circuit or short to ground.
symptoms: MIL illumination; Minor impact on emissions; No driveability issues
actions: Inspect wiring for breaks or corrosion; Check purge valve resistance; Replace purge valve
location: Near the fuel tank or charcoal canister

title: EVAP Purge Control Valve Circuit High
problem: The ECU detects a high voltage condition in the EVAP purge control valve circuit, indicating a potential short to voltage.
symptoms: MIL illumination; Minor impact on emissions; No driveability issues
actions: Inspect wiring for shorts to power; Check purge valve resistance; Replace purge valve
location: Near the fuel tank or charcoal canister

title: Fuel Temperature Sensor 'A' Circuit
problem: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the fuel temperature sensor circuit, leading to inaccurate fuel temperature readings which can affect fuel trim.
symptoms: Reduced fuel economy; Engine hesitation; MIL illumination
actions: Check sensor wiring and connector; Test sensor resistance; Replace fuel temperature sensor
column9: often integrated with the fuel pump assembly

title: Fuel Temperature Sensor 'A' Circuit Low
problem: The ECU receives a low voltage signal from the fuel temperature sensor, indicating an abnormally high fuel temperature or a circuit issue.
symptoms: Engine running rich; Decreased power; MIL illumination
actions: Inspect sensor wiring for shorts to ground; Test sensor resistance; Replace fuel temperature sensor
column9: often integrated with the fuel pump assembly

title: Fuel Temperature Sensor 'A' Circuit High
problem: The ECU receives a high voltage signal from the fuel temperature sensor, indicating an abnormally low fuel temperature or a circuit issue.
symptoms: Engine running lean; Hard starting when cold; MIL illumination
actions: Inspect sensor wiring for open circuits; Test sensor resistance; Replace fuel temperature sensor
column9: often integrated with the fuel pump assembly

title: Fuel Pump 'A' Control Circuit/Open
problem: The ECU detects an open circuit or electrical malfunction in the control circuit for the fuel pump, preventing the pump from being activated.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't start; No fuel pump prime; Loss of fuel pressure
actions: Check fuel pump relay and fuse; Inspect wiring from ECU to fuel pump relay; Test for power at fuel pump connector

title: Cylinder 1 Injector Circuit Low
problem: The ECU detects a low voltage condition in the fuel injector circuit for cylinder 1, indicating a potential short to ground or wiring issue.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough idle; Reduced power
actions: Check injector wiring for shorts to ground; Test injector resistance; Replace fuel injector

title: Cylinder 1 Injector Circuit High
problem: The ECU detects a high voltage condition in the fuel injector circuit for cylinder 1, indicating a potential open circuit or short to power.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough idle; Excessive fuel consumption
actions: Check injector wiring for opens or shorts to power; Test injector resistance; Replace fuel injector

title: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire Detected
affectedPart: Ignition System / Fuel System / Mechanical Engine
problem: The ECU detects misfires occurring in multiple or random cylinders, indicating a general engine combustion issue rather than a single component failure.
symptoms: Engine running rough; Lack of power; Excessive vibrations
actions: Check spark plugs and ignition coils; Inspect fuel pressure and injectors; Perform compression test

title: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected
affectedPart: Spark Plug / Ignition Coil / Fuel Injector (Cylinder 1)
problem: The ECU detects a specific misfire event occurring in cylinder 1, meaning that cylinder is not contributing to power output as expected.
symptoms: Engine running rough; Loss of power; Excessive vibrations from engine
actions: Check spark plug for damage or fouling; Test ignition coil for cylinder 1; Test fuel injector for cylinder 1

title: Serial Communication Link Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an error in the communication between various modules on the motorcycle's CAN bus network. This can affect multiple systems.
symptoms: Multiple warning lights on dashboard; Intermittent component operation; ECU communication failure
actions: Inspect CAN bus wiring for damage; Check connections to ECU and dashboard; Troubleshoot individual module power

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor 'A' Range/Performance
problem: The signal from the vehicle speed sensor is inconsistent or out of the expected range, affecting accurate speed readings.
symptoms: Erratic speedometer readings; Incorrect mileage; Cruise control malfunction (if equipped)
actions: Check VSS sensor for debris or damage; Inspect wiring harness for intermittent connection; Replace VSS
location: Rear wheel or transmission output shaft

title: Internal Control Module Random Access Memory (RAM) Error
problem: A critical internal error has been detected within the ECU's Random Access Memory, indicating a severe internal hardware or software fault.
symptoms: Engine won't start; Unpredictable engine behavior; MIL constantly on
actions: Check ECU power and ground; Attempt ECU re-flash (dealer tool); Replace ECU
location: Under seat or behind headlight fairing

title: ECM/PCM Processor Fault
problem: The ECU's internal processor has detected a fault in its own operation, which can lead to complete engine control failure.
symptoms: Engine won't start; Complete loss of engine power; Multiple unrelated codes
actions: Check ECU power and ground connections; Verify ECU software version; Replace ECU
location: Under seat or behind headlight fairing

title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit
problem: The ECU detects an electrical malfunction in the engine coolant temperature sensor circuit, leading to incorrect temperature readings. (Relevant for liquid-cooled models like Himalayan).
symptoms: Incorrect temperature gauge reading; Rich/lean running conditions; Hard starting
actions: Check ECT sensor wiring; Test sensor resistance; Replace ECT sensor

title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Low
problem: The ECU receives a low voltage signal from the ECT sensor, indicating an abnormally high engine temperature or a sensor short to ground.
symptoms: Overheating indication (false); Rich fuel mixture; Hard starting when hot
actions: Inspect ECT sensor wiring for shorts; Test sensor resistance; Replace ECT sensor

title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor High
problem: The ECU receives a high voltage signal from the ECT sensor, indicating an abnormally low engine temperature or an open circuit.
symptoms: Engine running cold (false); Lean fuel mixture; Increased emissions
actions: Inspect ECT sensor wiring for open circuits; Test sensor resistance; Replace ECT sensor

title: Vehicle Down Sensor Fault
problem: The ECU detects a fault in the lean angle sensor, often a general fault if the sensor is incorrectly installed or damaged, or its signal is intermittent.
symptoms: Engine not starting; Engine stalling unexpectedly; MIL illumination
actions: Verify LAS mounting and orientation; Check sensor wiring and connector; Replace LAS sensor
location: Often under the seat or behind the headlight

title: Engine Failed to Start
affectedPart: Starter Motor / Battery / Fuel System / Ignition System
problem: The ECU detects that the engine attempted to start but failed, indicating a fundamental issue preventing ignition or sustained combustion.
symptoms: Engine cranks but won't catch; No ignition; Repeated failed start attempts
actions: Check fuel pressure; Verify spark at plugs; Test battery and starter motor

title: Starter Relay Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the starter relay control circuit, preventing the starter motor from engaging.
symptoms: Engine won't crank; No click from starter relay; No power to starter motor
actions: Check starter relay fuse; Inspect starter relay wiring; Test or replace starter relay
